(1) COULD THE NEXT WORKER RUN measure.py WITH THE WORD RECORD AND GET ALL FIVE OBSERVABLES IN ONE CALL, OR RE-PLAN? Partially -- the DATA half is complete and would not need re-planning: DATASET_IDS, FIRST_RUN_DATASET_ID, FIRST_RUN_COMPANY, QUERY_ATTEMPTS (with STOP_RULE), OBSERVABLES, COST_CAP_USD/cost_cap_exceeded(), CANNOT_SERVE_SIGNAL and FOURTH_SURFACE_NOTE are all already module-level data compose_request() reads; the next worker's main() already accepts --word-record and clears the G-24 gate (main(), the 'if not args.word_record' branch) without needing to touch that logic. BUT it could NOT get all five observables in one call as this file stands: past the word-record gate, main() calls compose_request() and then only PRINTS the composed request and returns 4 -- it does not send anything, read a response, or compute any of the five OBSERVABLES (cost, field_schema, latency, freshness, cashtag_queryability), because no HTTP client exists in this module (AC4, deliberate). The next order must ADD: an HTTP client call using the composed request dict from compose_request(); a usage/billing read before/after for 'cost'; a wall-clock timer around the call for 'latency'; JSON parsing of the response for 'field_schema' and 'freshness'; and a call into lib.research.rules.item.qualify() per returned record for 'cashtag_queryability'. That is meaningful new code (an HTTP layer + observable extraction), not a one-line plug-in -- so the honest answer is: the PLAN (what to trigger, in what order, under what cap, with what stop rule) needs no re-planning, but the EXECUTION path (the client and the five observable readers) is not yet written and is new work for that order, consistent with AC4's bound and the worker face's own statement that 'the client is added by the order that carries the word'. (2) DOES THE STOP RULE PREVENT A SECOND TRIGGER IF THE FIRST ANSWERS 'CANNOT SERVE THE FEED'? AS DATA, yes: STOP_RULE and CANNOT_SERVE_SIGNAL both state the condition (all reachable QUERY_ATTEMPTS shapes exhausted with zero admitted records, or the next attempt's estimated cost would exceed COST_CAP_USD) as the point at which the run stops rather than re-triggering a shape already attempted. But AS CODE, this is NOT YET MECHANICALLY ENFORCED: no function in this module currently loops over QUERY_ATTEMPTS, checks a stop condition, or tracks which shapes have already been sent -- compose_request() builds exactly one request per call and main() calls it exactly once. The stop rule is fully SPECIFIED (in STOP_RULE's own string and in MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md s.2) but not yet IMPLEMENTED as a loop with a guard; the next order must write that loop and must not silently drop the guard while doing so. DECLARED WEAKEST LINK: the gap between 'the stop rule is stated as data' and 'the stop rule is enforced by running code' is exactly the kind of thing a later worker could get wrong by re-triggering shape 1 after shape 2 already stopped the run, if it does not carry the STOP_RULE string forward into an actual loop condition. Recorded for the CVO's own read, not self-graded.
